summary: PLAN_ITERATE complete after one full-fix iteration. Five parallel analyses (completeness, clarity/consistency, feasibility/parallelizability, testability, security/performance) produced 3 critical, 12 high, ~12 medium findings, strongly cross-confirmed (the opt-in contradiction was found independently by three analysts). All findings at or above the medium threshold are fixed; openspec validate --strict and validate_work_packages.py both pass. The headline architectural change is new design decision D13: forward enforcement opts in per contract document (D6, clarified), reverse enforcement opts in per capability via openspec/contracts/<capability>/traceability-exclusions.yaml — a file that is simultaneously the requirement-side exclusion home the plan was missing entirely (the schema could not express a requirement exclusion) and the opt-in switch that cannot be flipped without doing the triage it certifies. This resolves the contradiction that made task 5.2's staging infeasible and the flagship retrofit self-redding. IMPORTANT for PLAN_REVIEW: the gatekeeper's proposed wp-model fix (widen write_allow to regenerated artifacts) was investigated and is WRONG — the traceability field on archetype-only models (FlagSpec/PositionalSpec/ToolCommandSpec/OperationSpec, absent default) touches neither CI byte-identity gate; the correct fix (now in task 2.2 and wp-model) is the model-placement constraint, not write scope. Vendor review was deliberately NOT dispatched from within the skill because the orchestrator's PLAN_REVIEW phase runs it next; this is stated, not silent.

decisions.decision: D13: one opt-in switch per direction; the exclusions file IS the reverse switch
decisions.rationale: Three analysts independently confirmed the opt-in unit contradiction (spec said per contract AND per capability; D10 said per capability then per file ten lines apart). The per-capability reading breaks 5.2's staging (locks.yaml opt-in would demand triage of all 122 coordinator requirements) and self-reds the flagship (~31-48 gen-eval requirements dragged in by a 17-flag retrofit). Alternatives rejected: reverse-implied-by-any-document (adoption cliff), standalone boolean marker (flippable without doing the work). The exclusions file doubles as the requirement-exclusion home, so the design adds one artifact, not two. This does not reintroduce the second flag D12 struck — that was a reported-to-blocking flag for the SAME claim; D13 switches a different claim.

decisions.decision: Overrode the gatekeeper's suggested wp-model write_allow widening
decisions.rationale: generate_contract_schemas.py generates from InterfaceDescriptor/Scenario/GenEvalReport; FlagSpec/PositionalSpec/ToolCommandSpec/OperationSpec are not reachable from InterfaceDescriptor, and exclude_defaults=True keeps descriptor.yaml byte-identical for absent-default fields. The correct constraint is model placement, now written into task 2.2 and wp-model's description. Widening write scope would have licensed exactly the schema drift the CI gates exist to catch.

decisions.decision: Made undefined behavior deterministic instead of deleting the features
decisions.rationale: Concentration ('disproportionate'), scope wording, candidate lists, and malformed-input handling were all specified in judgement words. Each now has a deterministic observable (named constant, pinned output lines, top-5 bound, fail-closed requirement) while keeping the pass/fail judgement exactly where the original design put it — D7's report-not-fail stance is unchanged; only the OUTPUT became testable.

decisions.decision: Renumbered phase 3 rather than inserting suffixed task ids
decisions.rationale: Two new test tasks (requirement exclusions, malformed input) belong before the gate implementation. Clean ranges (3.1-3.16) keep work-package task references readable; the change is pre-implementation so nothing external breaks except the gatekeeper handoff's references, which are a historical record.

decisions.decision: Vendor review skipped inside the skill; orchestrator PLAN_REVIEW covers it
decisions.rationale: iterate-on-plan auto-enables vendor review in coordinated tier, but autopilot's next phase IS the multi-vendor plan review. Running it twice doubles cost for no information. Reported per the no-silent-fallback rule.
